title: Exhaust flow, catalyst efficiency and backpressure
whatItIs: The exhaust system must remove burned gases and the catalyst must store oxygen correctly. A catalyst code is not the same thing as a blocked exhaust, but both affect OBD graphs.
normalValues: A healthy catalyst has downstream O2 behavior damped relative to upstream after mixture control is stable. A healthy exhaust does not prevent MAF/load from rising during WOT.
deviations: P0420/P0430 should be judged only after misfire and mixture faults are addressed
High MAP with low MAF/load under WOT can indicate backpressure
Hot catalyst after misfire or rich running is a consequence, not always root cause
Exhaust leak before O2 can create false lean signals
influence: Blocked exhaust makes the engine feel choked. Catalyst efficiency faults are emissions faults and can be secondary to mixture, misfire or oil consumption.
checks: Measure exhaust backpressure when WOT airflow is low and MAP is high
Compare upstream/downstream O2 only in stable closed loop
Fix misfire and fuel trim faults before condemning catalyst
Inspect for exhaust leaks before the front sensor
